newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended lower, with Standard & Poor's 500 contracts sharpening their losses on concerns about a U.S. rate hike, traders and analysts said.
Concerns about higher rates did not stem from the U.S. Beige Book, which described price pressures in the U.S. as "temperate."
"This selloff has nothing to do with the Beige Book," one trader said about the U.S. Federal Reserve's summary of U.S. economic activity.
The book was released on Wednesday afternoon.
"You could say we are losing our irrational exuberance," a floor analyst said. "We are pricing in a possible rise in the discount rate."
March S&Ps plunged to 801.30, through support at 802.40. The contract had held that support level initially, as well as the 805.00 and 806.00 levels, before succumbing to local selling.
Traders said local, dealer and hedge fund selling was heavy in the pits throughout the afternoon, and they look for March S&Ps to break 800.00 in the near term.

Another floor source said the stage for the market's selloff was set Tuesday when the March contract closed at a discount to cash S&Ps. On Tuesday, March closed below its fair value, which was then pegged at 1.00 point above cash.
"That's bearish," he said. "It shows people are less discriminatory about prices and are looking to exit anywhere they can."

Once again, March S&Ps traded at a discount to the cash S&P index late on Wednesday. Fair value stood at about 0.80 point over cash, with arbitrage sell programs at a premium of 0.10 and arbitrage buy programs 1.50 over.
